items.title: ELEVATE NxT 2026–27 (DeepTech)

eligibility: Deep-tech startup as per DPIIT definition (up to 20 years old, turnover up to ₹300 Cr)
No ELEVATE grant received in the 3 years before 13 Oct 2026
Must relocate registered office to Karnataka if selected
benefits: One-time equity-free grant up to ₹1 Cr in milestones
Mentoring and incubation support
items.note: Closes 5:00 PM IST on 13 Nov 2026.

items.title: ELEVATE Minorities 2026
items.summary: Grant-in-aid for Karnataka-registered startups where a founder from a minority community holds at least 51% equity.
eligibility: Startup registered in Karnataka
At least 51% equity held by a minority-community founder
DPIIT recognition not required per the 2026 call
benefits: One-time grant up to ₹50 lakh
Mentoring support
items.note: Closes 5:00 PM IST on 13 Nov 2026. Applicants need at least 60 marks to reach the final pitch.

items.title: Grand Startup Challenge
items.org: CARS24 with Startup India & Startup Policy Forum
items.summary: National challenge putting early-stage startups on real problem statements across four tracks, with mentorship, deployment opportunities and a finale in New Delhi in January 2027.
eligibility: Early-stage Indian startups
Solution must fit one of the published track problem statements
benefits: Share of ₹1 Cr prize pool
Month of mentorship (Dec 2026)
Real deployment and investor visibility
items.note: Hard deadline 10 Nov 2026, 11:59 PM IST — organisers say it will not be extended.

items.title: UNDP–Generali MSME Insurance Innovation Challenge (India)
items.summary: Funding to develop or scale insurance products and services that are accessible, affordable and relevant for Indian MSMEs and their workers.
eligibility: Organisations with insurance / risk-protection solutions for Indian MSMEs
Solution should have a credible pathway to scale
benefits: Performance-based grant up to ~₹38.7 lakh
Access to UNDP and Generali expertise
items.note: Deadline 20 Nov 2026.

items.title: UNDP Ocean Innovation Challenge — 5th Call
items.summary: Implementation-ready solutions for marine pollution, coastal ecosystem restoration and a sustainable blue economy. Up to 10 winners.
eligibility: Legally registered private-sector organisations
Implementation-ready innovation
Preference for women-led and youth-led ventures; priority countries are Bangladesh, Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand and Viet Nam — check India eligibility in the call
benefits: Up to USD 100,000 via deliverable-based contract
Up to 17 months of incubation and mentoring
items.note: Closes 15 Nov 2026, 23:59 New York time.

items.title: Grassroot Innovation Programme 2026
items.summary: Grant for grassroots innovators in Karnataka building solutions to local, community-level problems.
eligibility: Innovators based in Karnataka
benefits: Grant up to ₹4 lakh
items.note: Deadline 23 Nov 2026, 5 PM. Link is a listing page — confirm on the KITS portal.

items.title: BE Hub Udaan — Accelerator Cohort 1
items.summary: 12-week acceleration programme for early-stage deep-tech and tech-led startups. Only 5–6 startups selected; starts 23 Nov 2026.
eligibility: Early-stage founders building deep-tech or tech-led startups
benefits: Idea and business-model validation
Industry network access
Growth preparation
items.note: Deadline 18 Nov 2026.

items.title: Hitachi Startup Challenge FY26
items.summary: 8-week programme to build a proof-of-concept plan with Hitachi business units in mobility and manufacturing; winners progress to a potential pilot.
eligibility: Companies worldwide with tech for transport or industrial operations
benefits: PoC co-development with Hitachi BUs
Potential pilot deal
items.note: Closes 8 Nov 2026, 11:59 PM GMT.

items.title: Techstars Accelerators 2027 (incl. Anywhere / London)

eligibility: Early-stage startups, any sector
benefits: USD 220K investment
Mentor network and demo day
items.note: Applications close 18 Nov 2026.

items.title: Ye! Youth Ecopreneurs Programme (YECO) 2026/27
items.summary: Global programme for young green entrepreneurs building land-restoration and environmental businesses.
eligibility: Founder / co-founder / CEO under 35 at the deadline
Green business with a scalable solution
benefits: Share of USD 100K prizes
All-expenses-paid trip to an international conference
Acceleration support
items.note: Deadline 22 Nov 2026. Link is a listing page — confirm on ITC's Ye! site.

items.title: Kotak BizLabs Accelerator — IIM Calcutta Innovation Park
items.summary: CSR accelerator for 20 early-revenue startups with social impact and a sustainability focus.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup
Early-revenue stage
Social impact / sustainability focus
benefits: Grant up to ₹30 lakh (milestone-based)
One-on-one mentoring from the IIMCIP network
items.note: Closes 31 Oct 2026.

items.title: BIRAC E-YUVA & Innovation Fellowships — 4th call 2026
items.summary: Fellowships at E-YUVA centres for students, postgraduates and PhDs turning biotech research into products and startups.
eligibility: UG teams, PG and PhD/postdoc innovators
Must work at a BIRAC E-YUVA centre
benefits: Monthly stipend + annual research grant
Incubation and venture-creation support
items.note: Closes 31 Oct 2026.

items.title: NIDHI-PRAYAS
items.summary: Prototype grant for innovators turning an idea into a working proof-of-concept, routed through DST-approved PRAYAS incubators.
eligibility: Individual innovators or early teams
Apply through a PRAYAS centre (incubator)
benefits: Up to ₹10 lakh for prototyping
Incubator lab and mentoring access
items.note: Rolling/periodic calls via individual PRAYAS centres.

items.title: NIDHI Seed Support System (NIDHI-SSS)
items.summary: Seed support for startups incubated at DST-backed TBIs, typically via convertible or equity-linked instruments.
eligibility: Incubated at a DST-supported TBI
Indian startup with a tech product
benefits: Seed funding up to ₹1 Cr
items.note: Apply through your incubator; each TBI runs its own window.

items.title: BIRAC Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG)
items.summary: BIRAC's flagship early-stage grant to take biotech ideas to proof-of-concept, managed through partner bio-incubators.
eligibility: Biotech / life-science innovation
Individuals or startups (DPIIT/company as per call)
benefits: Grant up to ₹50 lakh over ~18 months
Mentoring by BIG partners
items.note: Two calls a year; watch BIRAC's call-for-proposals page.

items.title: RKVY-RAFTAAR Agribusiness Incubation
items.summary: Grant-in-aid for agri and allied startups through RKVY-RAFTAAR agribusiness incubators (R-ABIs) across India.
eligibility: Agriculture / allied-sector startups
Selected through an R-ABI cohort
benefits: Pre-seed up to ₹5 lakh
Seed up to ₹25 lakh
Two-month incubation training
items.note: Cohort calls by individual R-ABIs (IARI Pusa, MANAGE, etc.).

items.title: iDEX — Innovations for Defence Excellence
items.summary: Defence India Startup Challenges (DISC) and open challenges where startups solve problem statements from the armed forces.
eligibility: Indian startups / MSMEs / individual innovators
Solution to a published defence problem statement
benefits: Grant up to ₹1.5 Cr
Path to procurement by the armed forces
items.note: New DISC rounds are released periodically.

items.title: MSME Innovative Scheme (Incubation)
items.org: Ministry of MSME via Host Institutes
items.summary: Funding to develop and nurture ideas into prototypes through approved Host Institutes (incubators).
eligibility: Individual innovators / MSMEs
Apply via an approved Host Institute
benefits: Up to ₹15 lakh per idea
items.note: Rolling via the MSME Innovative portal.

items.title: Kerala Startup Mission Grants (Idea → Scale-up)
items.summary: Stage-wise grants: Idea (₹3L), Productization (₹7L; ₹12L for women/transgender founders), Market Acceleration (₹10L), Scale-up (₹15L).
eligibility: Startups registered with KSUM / operating in Kerala
benefits: Stage-based equity-free grants
items.note: Periodic calls; check KSUM schemes page.

items.title: StartinUP Incentives (UP Startup Policy 2026)
items.amount: ₹20K/month for 2 yrs + up to ₹10L prototype + up to ₹15L seed
items.summary: Under UP Startup Policy 2026: sustenance allowance, a one-time prototype grant and seed capital for StartinUP-registered startups, plus free incubation for up to two years.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup
Registered and recognised on the StartinUP portal (Uttar Pradesh)
benefits: Sustenance allowance ₹20,000/month for 2 years
Prototype grant up to ₹10 lakh
Seed capital up to ₹15 lakh
Free incubation up to 2 years at recognised incubators/CoEs
items.note: Rolling. Detailed operational guidelines are published on the UP Startup Mission portal.

items.title: UP Startup Policy 2026 — Matching Grant
items.summary: Matches 50% of external capital raised by UP-recognised startups, capped at ₹5 crore.
eligibility: UP state-recognised startup
Prior fundraise of at least ₹2 crore
benefits: Matching grant up to ₹5 Cr
items.note: Open year-round. Confirm operational guidelines on the portal.

items.title: UP Grand Challenges Grant
items.summary: Open competitive calls under UP Startup Policy 2026; scaling-stage winners receive grant-in-aid.
eligibility: UP state-recognised startup
Scaling stage
benefits: Grant-in-aid up to ₹3 Cr
items.note: Challenges announced periodically.

items.title: Student Startup & Innovation Policy (SSIP 2.0)
items.summary: Proof-of-concept support for student and recent-graduate innovators in Gujarat institutions.
eligibility: Students / recent grads of Gujarat institutions
benefits: PoC grant up to ₹2.5 lakh
items.note: Rolling via institute SSIP cells.

items.title: i-Hub Gujarat — Startup Srujan
items.summary: Seed support (S4) under Gujarat's SSIP 2.0, implemented by i-Hub, for student and early-stage innovators.
eligibility: Student / young innovators from Gujarat's education ecosystem (under 35)
benefits: Grant ₹2.5L–₹10L
Incubation at i-Hub Ahmedabad
items.note: Rolling.

items.title: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS)
items.amount: Collateral-free loans, guarantee cover up to ₹20 crore
items.summary: Government guarantee on loans and venture debt from banks, NBFCs and AIF debt funds to DPIIT startups, so lenders need no collateral.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup
Stable revenue / not in default
benefits: Collateral-free debt
Guarantee cover up to ₹20 Cr per borrower
items.note: Apply through member lending institutions.

items.title: Technology Development Board — Funding
items.summary: Low-interest loans and equity support to commercialise indigenous technology; also runs bilateral calls (e.g. India–Finland).
eligibility: Indian company commercialising a technology
benefits: Soft loans at concessional interest
Equity / grant in select calls
items.note: Rolling applications plus periodic calls.

items.title: 100Unicorns Accelerator VC
items.summary: Accelerator VC giving seed funding and hands-on support to early-stage Indian startups from idea to angel stage.
eligibility: Early-stage Indian startups
benefits: Seed cheque
Mentoring and follow-on network
items.note: Always open.

items.title: Zero Shot Fund
items.summary: USD 100M fund backing AI-native founders in robotics, energy, automation, infrastructure, security and observability. No deck needed to start a conversation.
eligibility: Building an AI-native company
benefits: USD 1M–4M cheque
items.note: Rolling. Link is a listing page — find the fund's own apply form.

items.title: Y Combinator Winter 2027 Batch
items.summary: YC's three-month Winter 2027 batch (January–March) in San Francisco, open to founders anywhere in the world, with a US$500K investment in every accepted company.
eligibility: Startups from any country, including India — no US incorporation, visa or business licence needed to apply
Any stage, from idea to early revenue
Founders must be able to attend in person in San Francisco for the batch
One application per company; co-founders apply together
benefits: US$500,000 invested on acceptance
Three months of partner office hours and weekly in-person events
Demo Day access to a large investor audience
YC help with US incorporation and visas after acceptance
Lifetime access to the YC alumni network
items.note: On-time deadline is 2 Nov 2026 at 8:00 PM Pacific — about 9:30 AM IST on 3 Nov. YC still reviews late applications but gives no fixed response date. Expect to relocate to San Francisco for the batch; no application fee.

items.title: First in the World Challenge Grants 2026
items.amount: Up to ₹8 Cr (staged: ₹1 Cr / ₹4 Cr / ₹8 Cr)
items.summary: ICMR's high-risk, high-reward call for health technologies that have never been attempted anywhere in the world — new vaccines, drugs, diagnostics or interventions — funded in milestone-linked stages up to ₹8 crore.
eligibility: Indian startups, MSMEs and industry can apply alongside academic and research institutions
Government medical colleges, INIs, ICMR institutes, universities and recognised R&D labs
Private institutions and NGOs registered with DSIR as research organisations (NGOs must also be on NITI Aayog's DARPAN portal)
Each proposal needs one Principal Investigator plus at least one Co-PI from the same institution
Idea must be genuinely first-of-its-kind globally; incremental improvements are rejected
benefits: Proof-of-concept stage: up to ₹1 Cr over 2 years
Prototype stage: up to ₹4 Cr over 3 years
Final product/model stage: up to ₹8 Cr over 4 years
Non-dilutive funding released against deliverables, with a path to the next stage
items.note: Submit only on the ICMR e-PMS portal (epms.icmr.org.in) by 30 Nov 2026, 5:30 PM IST; results expected 31 Dec 2026. Incomplete proposals are rejected before review. Selected teams must later provide an institutional undertaking, ethics (IEC) approval where relevant, and bank details.

items.title: Hello Tomorrow Global Challenge 2026–27
items.amount: €200K investment for the top pitch + in-kind prizes
items.summary: Free-to-enter global deep-tech competition with 12 tracks; around 800 startups become Deep Tech Pioneers, about 90 finalists pitch at the Amsterdam summit in June 2027, and the winner pitch carries a €200K investment from DeepBright Ventures.
eligibility: Deep-tech startups built on new technology, a scientific discovery or complex engineering
Stage: proof of concept or prototype up to Series B
Team of at least two people
Not a subsidiary or spin-off of an existing company
Market application expected within 15 years; incorporation not needed to apply
benefits: Deep Tech Pioneer status and Investor Day meetings with 300+ VCs and CVCs
Finalists pitch for a €200K investment from DeepBright Ventures
Track-winner coaching and investor, partner and customer introductions
Corporate-track pitching slots and prizes
items.note: Applications close 30 Nov 2026 and are free. Pioneers are notified late Jan–early Feb 2027; finalists in mid-March. Summit tickets need a refundable €99 deposit, and travel and accommodation to Amsterdam are not covered. Prize funds are only paid once the startup is incorporated.

items.title: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes (VCF-ST)
items.org: Ministry of Tribal Affairs, managed by IFCI Venture Capital Funds
items.summary: A ₹50 crore government-anchored fund that backs Scheduled Tribe-owned businesses and startups, mainly through convertible or non-convertible debentures, with limited equity for innovative tech startups.
eligibility: Company at least 51% owned and managed by Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs
Ownership and control held for 6 months (up to ₹50 lakh) or 12 months (above ₹50 lakh)
Manufacturing, services or allied sectors, including TBI-incubated startups; projects must create assets
A new company can qualify as successor to an eligible proprietorship, partnership, OPC or LLP
Documentary proof of ST status required; women-led ventures preferred for at least 30% of support
benefits: ₹10 lakh to ₹5 crore, capped at twice the company's net worth
TBI-selected tech projects: up to ₹10 lakh a year for 3 years
Instruments include CCDs, OCDs and NCDs; equity up to 49% for innovative tech startups
Government-anchored capital with screening via NSTFDC
items.note: Rolling scheme with no fixed closing date. Funding is mostly debt-style debentures, so expect repayment or conversion terms; assistance is limited to twice your net worth. Applications are sourced through NSTFDC and IFCI Venture — contact them for the current application route.

items.title: National Startup Awards 6.0 (2026)
items.org: DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Startup India)
items.summary: The government's flagship startup awards are back with a much bigger purse: ₹25 lakh for the winner in each of 20 sector categories and two special categories, up from ₹10 lakh last edition. A separate ₹25 lakh pool covers school and college student innovators.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup (private limited company, registered partnership or LLP)
Not more than 10 years old from the date of incorporation
Annual turnover never above ₹100 crore in any financial year
Not under insolvency proceedings; past NSA winners cannot re-apply
Student Innovator track: school/college students (individual or team of up to 4) with a prototype, MVP or proof of concept; DPIIT recognition not needed
benefits: ₹25 lakh cash prize per winning category (20 sectoral + Women-Led Startup of the Year + North-East Startup Excellence)
Student track prizes from ₹2 lakh to ₹6 lakh across four age groups
Mentoring, investor connects, market access and corporate tie-ups
National visibility and priority at DPIIT-backed startup events in India and abroad
items.note: Applications opened 27 Oct 2026 and close 20 Nov 2026 per DPIIT's launch announcement (one aggregator shows 30 Nov — treat 20 Nov as the safe date). Keep your DPIIT certificate and recent financial statements ready; check the portal for the full category rules and how many categories you may enter.

items.title: Start Up Energy Transition (SET) Award 2027
items.summary: A long-running global competition for energy and climate-tech startups, run by Germany's national energy agency. Five category winners take equity-free prize money, and finalists get a stage at the SET Tech Festival in Berlin in front of investors and corporates.
eligibility: Company founded in August 2016 or later, registered or in the process of registering
Past the idea stage with at least a proof of concept
Must have a client, an institutional/corporate partner, or a working prototype (hardware generally TRL 4+)
Apply to only one of the five categories; full application and attachments in English
Open to startups worldwide, including India
benefits: €10,000 equity-free prize for each category winner
Showcase and networking at the SET Tech Festival in Berlin
Media visibility through dena's international network
Introductions to energy-sector investors and corporate partners
items.note: Closes 30 Nov 2026 (Central European time — submit by the evening of 30 Nov IST to be safe). Late or partially completed applications are rejected. Categories: Clean Energy & Storage; Digital Energy, Markets & Economy; Buildings & Construction; Industry & Value Chains; Mobility & Transportation. No application fee mentioned.

items.title: Telangana Innovation Startup Challenge (TISC) 2026
items.summary: Telangana is asking startups to solve seven concrete public-sector problems — led by low-cost solar irrigation for deep borewells — with the reward being paid government pilots that can turn into long-term procurement contracts. Shortlisted teams will be showcased at the Invest Telangana Global Summit in December 2026.
eligibility: Startups, innovators, researchers, technology firms and academic institutions
Applicants from anywhere in India (and international innovation centres) may apply
Solution must address one of the seven listed problem statements
Judged on problem relevance, originality, technology readiness, team capability and impact
benefits: Pilot deployment with Telangana government departments
Route to long-term government procurement contracts, subject to pilot results
Showcase slot at the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026 (Bharat Future City, December)
Direct engagement with state officials on real-world problems
items.note: Deadline 30 Nov 2026. The seven challenges: solar irrigation pumps/retrofit kits for deep borewells (~30% cheaper, theft-resistant panels, tamper-proof metering); rapid food-adulteration testing for hostels; satellite monitoring of lake and land encroachment; automated pothole mapping and repair; needle-free anaemia screening; AI-based Telugu reading assessment; satellite/app-based crop mapping. No cash prize announced — the value is the pilot and contract pathway.

items.title: MassChallenge Challenge Programs 2026–27
items.summary: A five-month, partner-matched accelerator in which pre-seed to Series A startups work directly with a large corporate on that company's published problem statement, aiming for a pilot or commercial deal. Tracks this cycle cover climate, security and resiliency, fintech, healthcare and sustainable food systems.
eligibility: Pre-seed to Series A startups based anywhere in the world (Boston residency not required)
Your solution must answer at least one partner's published challenge statement
At least one founder or C-suite member must attend the in-person Boston sessions
Able to commit roughly 3–5 hours a week from February to June 2027
benefits: Matched collaboration with a corporate partner (past partners include Deloitte, Eli Lilly, Sanofi, Verizon, MassMutual, SharkNinja)
Regular partner meetings aimed at a pilot or commercial agreement
Mentors across marketing, legal, investment, compliance and technology
Entry into the MassChallenge alumni and investor network
items.note: Applications close 9 Nov 2026 (no closing time given, so assume US Eastern and submit early). Finalists hear in December; matchmaking is 6–8 Jan 2027 and kickoff 9–10 Feb 2027 in Boston. Indian founders should budget for travel and US visas for the mandatory in-person events; equity and fee terms are not stated on the official page.

items.title: Microsoft Imagine Cup 2027
items.amount: Up to USD 5K Azure credits + prizes
items.summary: Microsoft's global AI startup competition, now run as seven categories including a dedicated Student Startup track. Teams build on Microsoft Cloud and AI, and category winners and finalists advance to a World Championship.
eligibility: Every team member must be at least 18 and register individually; teams of up to four
The startup must be a registered legal entity founded on or after 2 November 2024
Must not have raised Series C or later funding; past Imagine Cup winners cannot re-enter
Not based in or operating from US-sanctioned regions (India is eligible)
Student-led startups can enter the Student Startup category
benefits: Up to USD 5,000 in Azure credits for registered teams to build an MVP
Category winner and Top 20 Startup recognition
Finalists and the Student Prize winner pitch at the World Championship
Visibility with Microsoft for Startups and its partner network
items.note: Submissions close 11:59 pm US Central Time on 28 Feb 2027 (about 11:29 am IST on 1 Mar). You cannot edit after submitting. Cash prize amounts are not listed on the official FAQ, and the Official Rules override the FAQ, so read them before entering.

items.title: MedTech Innovator 2027 Accelerator
items.amount: Share of USD 700K+ prizes (top prize USD 350K)
items.summary: A five-month, mentor-led accelerator for medical device, diagnostics and digital health companies that ends in a public prize competition. Non-US startups, including Indian ones, are welcome as long as they plan to enter the US market.
eligibility: Building a medical device, diagnostic or digital health product
Early to mid-stage, with clinical validation in progress or on the horizon
A founder or C-suite leader must commit to the full five-month programme
Companies outside the US can apply but need a clear US market strategy
No fee to apply
benefits: Mentor matching with industry leaders and access to investors
Early-stage track competes for USD 350K and mid-stage track for USD 250K at the finals, plus extra awards
Showcase at The MedTech Conference
Partner resources and in-kind services through the programme
items.note: Applications close 1 Dec 2026 (US time, so submit by 30 Nov in India to be safe). Applying is free, but selected companies pay a USD 15,000 programme fee in cash or as a USD 50K SAFE. Scholarships exist, and some specialty tracks require a USD 50K SAFE. Expect US travel for in-person events.

items.title: BioTools Innovator 2027 Accelerator
items.amount: Up to USD 250K grand prize (USD 300K+ pool)
items.summary: A non-profit accelerator and prize competition for companies building life science research tools, diagnostics, software and services used by drug developers. Startups headquartered anywhere, including India, can apply if they have a US go-to-market plan.
eligibility: Life science tools, diagnostics, software or services for drug developers (drug, biologic, cell and gene therapy developers are out of scope)
Pre-seed to Series B, with a prototype and proof of concept in hand or close to it
Raised no more than USD 25M in equity
International companies welcome with a clear US market strategy
Must be incorporated before the programme starts and attend two mandatory in-person events
benefits: USD 250K for the finals winner, USD 25K for each of up to four finalists and USD 10K for the best video
Mentorship from corporate partners, workshops and investor pitching
A BARDA-backed VANGUARD track for up to ten biotools startups, with its programme fee fully covered
items.note: Closes 1 Dec 2026; no closing time is published, so submit a few days early. No application fee, but accepted companies pay USD 15,000 (cash, two instalments, or a USD 50K SAFE) unless they win a scholarship or join VANGUARD.

items.title: SusHi Tech Challenge 2027 (Tokyo pitch contest)
items.summary: The global startup pitch competition at SusHi Tech Tokyo 2027, Asia's large innovation conference run by the Tokyo government, with a JPY 10 million grand prize. It looks for startups whose technology helps build sustainable, resilient cities.
eligibility: Startups with a new technology or business model and real growth potential
Must already have a product or service in the market
Business should fit the theme of sustainable cities through technology (e.g. physical AI, quantum, resilience, longevity, drug discovery)
Must be able to pitch in person in Tokyo on both event days and staff a booth for all three days (20–22 May 2027)
benefits: JPY 10 million for the grand prize winner
Semifinalists get the JPY 300,000 booth fee waived and a networking session
Planned special awards from corporate partners
Exposure to investors, corporates and the Tokyo government
items.note: Closes 5:00 pm JST on 18 Dec 2026 (1:30 pm IST). Travel to Tokyo is at your own cost; the page mentions no travel support. Read the official application guidelines for any further conditions.

items.title: Social Startups Programme (Cohort 1)
items.amount: ₹45K/month for 8 months, then ₹15–20 lakh/yr seed grant for 2 yrs
items.summary: A new Azim Premji Foundation programme for experienced development professionals who want to found and lead their own grassroots non-profit. About 100 people get a paid eight-month seeding phase to set up the organisation in Odisha, the North-East, Eastern UP or Bengaluru Urban, with a two-year seed grant open to those who hit their milestones.
eligibility: Under 40 years of age
Graduate degree
At least 3 years of ground-level work in the development sector
Must intend to set up and lead a new civil society organisation as a first-time founder
Not already a founder or co-founder of any registered organisation
Willing to relocate to and commit long-term to one of the four focus geographies
benefits: Monthly honorarium of ₹45,000 during the 8-month seeding phase (from 1 April 2027)
One-month residential boot camp and supported fieldwork
Hands-on help with registration, governance, compliance, finance, HR and programme design
Pathway to a two-year grant of ₹15–20 lakh per year for those who meet milestones
items.note: Applications close 31 Dec 2026. This is for founding a non-profit, not a for-profit startup. Selection: screening, document review, statement of purpose, online interview and in-person panel; results expected by Feb 2027. Focus themes include rural livelihoods, health, youth, disability, child welfare, Adivasi well-being and urban informal settlements.

items.title: UNICEF Femtech Ventures – Call 2.0
items.amount: Up to US$100,000 equity-free + 12 months mentoring
items.summary: UNICEF's Venture Fund is backing early-stage for-profit companies that use frontier technology to improve the health of women and girls. Selected startups receive equity-free funding plus a year of technical support, in exchange for making their solution open source.
eligibility: Registered private for-profit company (NGOs, universities and individuals cannot apply)
Registered in a UNICEF programme country — check UNICEF's country list
Working prototype that has already produced some initial data
Frontier-tech solution (e.g. AI, data science, blockchain) benefiting vulnerable girls and women
Willing to release the solution under an open-source licence
benefits: Up to US$100,000 in equity-free funding
12 months of technical mentorship
Access to UNICEF's global network and country offices
Founders keep all other IP — the open-source code is UNICEF's only 'return'
items.note: Closes 11 Nov 2026. Funded companies must have an OSI-approved (or equivalent) open-source licence in place by month six. Women-led teams and founders under 35 are strongly encouraged.

items.title: D-Prize Global Competition 2026–27
items.summary: D-Prize gives first-time social entrepreneurs seed money to launch a venture that delivers an already-proven poverty intervention — such as ORS for childhood diarrhoea, reading glasses, water filters or post-harvest support — to people who still lack it. You pick one of its listed challenges (or propose your own) and pitch a distribution model you can pilot quickly.
eligibility: New ventures only: typically under 18 months of full-time operation and under US$30,000 raised
Existing organisations considered only if their core work is distributing an evidence-based poverty intervention
Must target one of D-Prize's challenge areas or a well-argued 'propose your own' intervention
Founders from low- and middle-income countries such as India are especially encouraged
Willing to run a pilot and then raise follow-on funding to scale
benefits: Up to US$20,000 to launch and pilot the venture
Ongoing guidance from the D-Prize team during the pilot
Credibility with follow-on funders after a successful pilot
Light first round — only a two-page concept note and CVs
items.note: Regular round closes 15 Nov 2026 at midnight Pacific Time (about 1:30 PM IST on 16 Nov). A final extension deadline of 6 Dec 2026 is available only if you register for it on D-Prize's extension page. Round 1 needs a two-page concept note plus resumes; the top ~5% get two weeks to answer written questions, then interviews. Only around the top 1% of applicants are funded.

items.title: The Liveability Challenge 2027
items.amount: Up to S$1 million funding per winner
items.summary: A global search for scalable, commercially viable solutions to urban sustainability problems in tropical cities, run across three tracks: Decarbonisation, Cool Earth (resilience and cooling) and Oceans. Top solutions win grant funding and a pitch slot at the Grand Finale in Singapore during Ecosperity Week 2027.
eligibility: Open to startups and ventures worldwide, including India
Solution must address one of the three tracks: Decarbonisation, Cool Earth or Oceans
Must be scalable and commercially viable, with relevance to cities in the tropics
Early-stage to growth-stage companies with a working technology or business model are best placed
benefits: Up to S$1 million in grant funding for top solutions in each track
Decarbonisation finalists can be considered for up to S$2 million in development funding from A*STAR
Oceans finalists can be considered for up to S$500,000 equity investment from the Asia Ocean Fund
Pitch at the Grand Finale in Singapore before investors and corporates
items.note: Submissions close 18 Feb 2027 (check the portal for the exact time, usually Singapore time). The core prize is grant funding, but the A*STAR and Asia Ocean Fund add-ons are separate — the Asia Ocean Fund route is an equity investment. Finalists are expected to attend the Grand Finale in Singapore.

items.title: PRIP Scheme – Second Call (Pharma & MedTech R&D)
items.org: Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers
items.amount: Up to ₹5 Cr (early stage) / ₹100 Cr (later stage)
items.summary: The second call of the ₹5,000 crore Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma & MedTech (PRIP) scheme funds startups, MSMEs and industry building new drugs, biosimilars and novel medical devices. Early-stage projects start with a short concept note; later-stage projects apply directly with a detailed proposal.
eligibility: Early-stage track: startups and MSMEs taking a product from TRL 1–3 up to (not beyond) TRL 5
Later-stage track: industry, startups and MSMEs taking a product from TRL 4–6 to higher readiness
Project must fall in a priority area: new chemical/biological entities, phyto-pharmaceuticals, complex generics, biosimilars, or novel medical devices not yet approved by CDSCO
Projects already submitted in PRIP Round 1 should not be resubmitted
Ecosystem enablers (incubators etc.) may submit early-stage concept notes on behalf of startups in their network
benefits: Up to ₹5 crore per early-stage project
Up to ₹100 crore per later-stage project, covering up to 35% of approved project cost
Mentorship for commercialisation, plus MedTech Mitra and Patent Mitra support
Access to a collaboration platform linking industry, academia and startups
items.note: Submission window opened on the PRIP portal from mid-September 2026; no closing date has been announced, so apply early and check the portal. Later-stage awards need the applicant to co-fund at least 65% of the project. Novel device categories include AI/ML devices and SaMD/SiMD, genetic diagnostics, surgical robotics, telemedicine-enabled devices and novel IVDs/biomarkers.

items.title: Startup Buildathon India 2026 (Google AI)
items.org: Hack2skill with nasscom and HeadStart, alongside Google DeepMind and Google Cloud
items.summary: A multi-city build sprint for early AI startups and would-be founders, ending in a Grand Finale at Google in Bengaluru. Ten winning teams each take home $5,000 in cash plus $5,000 in Google AI and Cloud credits.
eligibility: Early-stage startups working on a new product idea, or aspiring founders with a startup idea
Solo founders and teams of two or more can apply
The product must be AI-powered
Shortlisted teams must attend an in-person city buildathon in one of ten Indian cities on 20–21 November
benefits: $10,000 per top-10 team: $5,000 cash and $5,000 in Google AI/Cloud credits (subject to taxes and terms)
Access to Google experts and mentors during the build
Route into Google startup support programmes
Pitch slots at regional showcases (Gurugram, Mumbai, Hyderabad) and the Bengaluru finale on 2 December
items.note: Applications close 13 November 2026 (no closing time published — submit by the evening before to be safe). Selected teams are told by 18 November. City buildathons run 20–21 November in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Kochi, Kolkata, Mumbai and Pune; you must travel to your city round at your own cost. Judging weighs founder profile, product potential, market viability, technical architecture and how well you use Google AI.

items.title: NLDSL DigiTwin Grand Challenge 2026
items.org: NICDC Logistics Data Services Ltd (NLDSL) with NICDC and DPIIT Startup India
items.amount: ₹3 lakh per sector winner; ₹20–30 lakh+ pool
items.summary: A government-backed contest to build digital twins of Indian logistics systems — ports, rail and road corridors, warehousing, mining and EV supply chains — using simulated datasets and the ULIP API platform. Stage 1 asks only for team registration and a concept note.
eligibility: Open to students, startups, enterprises, academic and research institutions, and independent innovators based in India
Teams of 2 to 5 members
At least one member must have hands-on skills in data engineering, AI/ML, GIS, modelling/simulation or software development
No participation fee
Teams may enter both the DigiTwin and the Freight Transport Model themes as separate applications
benefits: ₹3 lakh for the best team in each of six DigiTwin tracks (multimodal logistics; industrial corridors, parks and warehousing; mining and minerals; urban mobility and EV logistics; pharma/health/agri supply chains; open category)
Access to simulated logistics datasets and optional official ULIP APIs during prototyping
Demo to a national Grand Jury in January 2027
Winners may be enlisted as vendors with NLDSL
items.note: Stage 1 (registration + concept note) closes 14 November 2026. Shortlists follow on 22 November; Stage 2 detailed ideas are due 8 December; prototypes are built 10–31 December; jury demos run 4–14 January 2027. The organiser calls the timeline indicative. IP terms are in the full guidelines — read them before submitting. Help desk: support.digitaltwingc@nldsl.in.

items.title: AI for Good Innovation Factory 2026–27
items.org: ITU (UN International Telecommunication Union) – AI for Good
items.summary: The UN's AI for Good platform runs monthly online pitch rounds from September 2026 to May 2027 for startups using AI against global development challenges. Winners of each round progress towards a Grand Finale at the AI for Good Global Summit in Geneva, where the top startup wins $20,000.
eligibility: Startups worldwide (Indian founders included) with an AI-powered solution
The solution should address one or more UN Sustainable Development Goals
The AI must be central, innovative and able to scale
A working product or pilot strengthens your chances in the live pitch rounds
benefits: $20,000 cash prize for the overall winner
Live online pitch sessions in front of experts, investors and UN agencies
Startup Accelerator Programme in Geneva, 21–24 June 2027, for finalists
Global visibility through the AI for Good Global Summit
items.note: Applications run through ITU's Innovation Factory startup form and feed a series of monthly pitching sessions until May 2027, so apply early to get a slot (one listing names 23 November 2026 for the next intake). The pre-final is on 22 June 2027 and the Grand Finale on 24 June 2027 in Geneva — travel costs aren't stated. ITU warns it is not linked to any paid pitch-coaching services offering 'guaranteed' entry.

items.title: ACHEMA Start-up Award 2027
items.summary: A business-plan competition for young companies and founding teams in chemistry, process engineering and biotechnology, run by the organiser of ACHEMA, the world's largest process-industry trade fair. Up to ten finalists exhibit at ACHEMA 2027 in Frankfurt and the winner receives €15,000.
eligibility: Teams or individuals with a company concept or business plan, or companies founded after 1 January 2024
Venture must be in chemistry, process technology or biotechnology
Product or service must be a market innovation with a clear competitive advantage, explained in the plan
Entries in English or German; at least one named person as founder/contact
No nationality restriction is stated in the terms
benefits: €15,000 prize money for the winner, presented on stage at ACHEMA 2027
Mentors and venture capitalists assigned from the start
Free showcase space for up to ten finalists during ACHEMA, 14–18 June 2027
Jury pitch in February 2027 and exposure to global process-industry buyers
items.note: Full business plans must be submitted by 30 November 2026, along with a signed copy of the terms and conditions. Finalists are picked in January 2027 and must present in person in Frankfurt (February jury pitch and June fair) — budget for travel. File patents before submitting, as plans are shared with jurors and mentors under NDA.

items.title: Nexa Lighthouse — Climate & Health Innovation Call (Asia-Pacific)
items.org: Grand Challenges Canada and AVPN, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation
items.summary: Nexa Lighthouse funds proven, locally led innovations in Asia and the Pacific that help health systems act on climate risks such as extreme heat, air pollution and shifting malaria/dengue patterns. A linked South Asia call focuses on protecting people with diabetes and heart disease from extreme heat.
eligibility: Incorporated organisations based in Asia-Pacific (India included): companies, social enterprises, NGOs, non-profits, research institutions or government bodies
Individuals, sole proprietorships, unincorporated trusts and partnerships cannot apply
Innovation must already be proven and ready to scale — this is not early-idea money
Solution must be locally led and address a climate-linked health threat (heat, air quality, vector-borne disease)
benefits: Transition to Scale investment of roughly $250,000 to $2 million per innovation, sized by maturity
Backing from Grand Challenges Canada and AVPN's network of Asian funders
Support to embed the solution with local health actors and systems
items.note: Proposals are due 17 November 2026 at 2:00 pm ET (12:30 am IST on 18 November) via Grand Challenges Canada's Fluxx portal — apply through that portal, not the Novo Nordisk Foundation, or you risk disqualification. Funding instrument (grant vs. repayable/equity-linked) is set at the partners' discretion. The South Asia cardiometabolic-heat strand must be framed around heat protection for patients, not general climate adaptation.
